sections.text:
Collective estimation under unreliable sensing requires robots to adaptively balance personal observations and social information from peers. We propose DGF-Asym, a decentralized collective estimation method extending the DeGroot-Friedkin model with asymmetric peer weighting based on retrospective predictive performance.

The method supports consensus formation without prior sensor-noise statistics or explicit fault models while keeping inter-robot communication asynchronous. We evaluate DGF-Asym in simulated collective navigation under noisy observations and time-varying sensor faults.

Compared with three baselines, it produces more stable estimates and more reliably sustains the decision criterion, at the cost of longer decision times. However, overall performance depends on fault ratio, group size, and influence-threshold selection.

Our results demonstrate the potential of adaptive peer weighting for stable model-free collective estimation under unreliable sensing.

summary.en: The paper proposes DGF-Asym, a decentralized collective estimation method that extends the DeGroot-Friedkin model by adapting asymmetric peer weights according to retrospective predictive performance. It requires neither prior sensor-noise statistics nor explicit fault models, and supports asynchronous communication. In simulated collective navigation with noisy observations and time-varying sensor faults, the method yields more stable estimates and more reliably sustains the decision criterion than three baselines, but takes longer to decide. Performance also depends on fault ratio, group size, and influence-threshold selection.
summary.zh: 论文提出DGF-Asym，一种基于DeGroot-Friedkin模型的分布式集体估计方法，通过回顾预测表现来非对称地调整同伴权重。该方法无需预先掌握传感器噪声统计或明确故障模型，并支持异步机器人通信。作者在带噪观测和时变传感器故障的模拟集体导航中进行评估：与三个基线相比，估计更稳定，也更可靠地维持决策准则，但决策耗时更长。总体表现还受故障比例、群体规模和影响阈值选择影响。

items.title: DGF-Asym: Adaptive Peer Weighting for Collective Estimation under Noisy and Faulty Sensing

sections.text:
Failures in long-horizon embodied tasks can arise from how a vision-language-action model (VLA) is called or from its execution capabilities.

We introduce AdaRSI, an on-demand recursive self-improvement framework in which a coding agent first refines its tools and procedures, then adapts sub-steps that remain unreliable after testing alternative instructions and approaches.

The agent collects demonstrations, tests their utility through temporary fine-tuning probes, and pools accepted data across tasks to train a specialist VLA that works alongside the original executor. At the end of each development round, its records are summarized into shared experience that guides subsequent diagnosis and data collection.

On unseen composite tasks in RoboCasa365, AdaRSI raises success from 4.6% to 13.3%.On perturbed LIBERO-Pro 2.0 tasks, success rises from 32.9% to 49.1%.On RoboCasa365's Composite-Unseen suite, it achieves higher success than adapting every manipulation sub-step, using 34% of the GPU time and 36% of the demonstrations.

On a real robot, the agent autonomously collects demonstrations and adapts the executor to recover fallen bottles, improving task completion.

summary.en: The paper presents AdaRSI, an on-demand recursive self-improvement framework for embodied agents. A coding agent first improves tools and procedures, then revises unreliable sub-steps after testing alternative instructions and approaches. It collects demonstrations, probes their value through temporary fine-tuning, and pools accepted data to train a specialist VLA alongside the original executor. The authors report higher success on specified simulation benchmarks, with reduced GPU time and demonstrations in one comparison. A real-robot demonstration addresses recovery of fallen bottles.
summary.zh: 论文提出 AdaRSI，一种面向具身智能体的按需递归自我改进框架：编码智能体先改进工具和流程，再针对测试后仍不可靠的子步骤调整指令与方法。系统收集示范，通过临时微调探测其效用，汇集各任务中认可的数据，训练与原执行器协同工作的专用 VLA，并将每轮记录整理为共享经验。在 RoboCasa365 未见组合任务和受扰动的 LIBERO-Pro 2.0 任务中，作者报告成功率有所提高；在 RoboCasa365 的 Composite-Unseen 测试中，报告其成功率高于逐一适配操作子步骤的方案，同时使用更少 GPU 时间和示范数据。真实机器人实验中，智能体自主收集示范并调整执行器，以恢复倒下的瓶子并提高任务完成情况。

items.title: AdaRSI: On-Demand Recursive Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents

sections.text:
Human cognitive state (e.g., distraction, stress), gaze, and behavior interact with the driving environment in subtle ways that AI could use to assist drivers, but ground-truth labels for human cognitive state levels are costly to obtain at scale.

We propose a multimodal masked-diffusion autoencoder, ID-MAE, that adds a self-supervised objective to impairment prediction: alongside predicting the impairment label as a masked token, it reconstructs masked gaze and trajectory.

To probe the effects of different modalities and types of impairments on model inference, we introduce DIVERT, a driving-simulator dataset containing 103 hours of driving data (n = 109) with ten impairment inductions spanning cognitive, visual, and emotional states, recorded with gaze, vehicle state, and scene video.

We demonstrate how ID-MAE affords significant improvements in impairment inference results on both the DIVERT dataset and existing datasets, and enables strong results in additional tasks, such as trajectory and gaze prediction.

For location-matched pairs, our model achieves a paired AUC of 0.706 for impairment detection on DIVERT, compared to 0.590 without reconstruction loss, improving over existing baselines. We probe the design space in terms of input modalities, masking scheme, positional encoding, attention mechanism, and decoding.

We also investigate the interaction between various impairments in training and inference, demonstrating that visually demanding distractions are separable from cognitive distractions. Code and data will be available upon acceptance.

summary.en: The paper proposes ID-MAE, a multimodal masked-diffusion autoencoder for modeling impairment in driving. Along with predicting an impairment label, it reconstructs masked gaze and trajectory as a self-supervised objective. The authors introduce DIVERT, a driving-simulator dataset recording gaze, vehicle state, and scene video across cognitive, visual, and emotional impairment inductions. They report improved impairment inference on DIVERT and existing datasets, and strong results for trajectory and gaze prediction. Their analyses also indicate that visually demanding distractions are separable from cognitive distractions.
summary.zh: 论文提出 ID-MAE，一种用于驾驶受损状态建模的多模态掩码扩散自编码器。模型在预测受损标签的同时重建被遮蔽的注视信息和轨迹，以利用自监督目标。作者还介绍 DIVERT，这是包含驾驶模拟器数据的数据集，记录注视、车辆状态和场景视频，并涵盖认知、视觉及情绪方面的多种状态诱发。作者报告，ID-MAE 在 DIVERT 及既有数据集上的受损状态推断结果有所改善，也能用于轨迹和注视预测；在 DIVERT 的位置匹配样本上，加入重建损失时配对 AUC 高于不加该损失的结果。作者还报告，视觉要求高的分心与认知分心可以区分。

items.title: Multimodal Masked Diffusion Autoencoder for Modeling Impaired Driving

sections.text:
Large-scale robotic simulation requires diverse deformable objects with executable physical properties and realistic interaction behaviors. However, existing 3D asset collections primarily emphasize visual diversity, while scalable physical construction and verification remain challenging.

We introduce RFW-S, a large-scale dataset of 83,365 simulation-verified assets spanning 485 everyday categories across five structural families: soft solids, cloth sheets, shells, garments, and bags.

We develop an automated pipeline integrating reference-guided 3D generation, structure-aware physical modeling, and LLM-assisted parameter estimation and calibration.

To ensure physical reliability, we introduce an independent simulation verification framework that evaluates object behaviors under interactions distinct from those used for parameter calibration. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of independent verification and characterize deformable responses under different physical configurations.

We further evaluate robotic grasping in terms of both task success and object integrity, and demonstrate the physical realism of our simulated objects through sim-to-real replay of fragile-object manipulation. RFW-S provides a scalable foundation for physically grounded simulation and embodied robotic learning.

summary.en: The paper introduces RFW-S, a dataset of simulation-verified everyday deformable objects for robotic simulation. Its assets span five structural families, including soft solids, cloth, shells, garments, and bags. The authors describe an automated pipeline combining reference-guided 3D generation, structure-aware physical modeling, and language-model-assisted parameter estimation and calibration. An independent simulation framework evaluates behaviors under interactions distinct from calibration. The paper reports experiments on verification, deformable responses, robotic grasping and object integrity, and sim-to-real replay of fragile-object manipulation.
summary.zh: 论文介绍 RFW-S，一个面向机器人仿真的可变形日常物体数据集，包含经仿真验证的资产，覆盖软固体、布片、壳体、服装和袋子五类结构。其自动化流程结合参考引导的三维生成、结构感知物理建模，以及由大语言模型辅助的参数估计与校准。作者提出独立仿真验证框架，在不同于参数校准所用的交互条件下评估物体行为，并报告实验展示了该验证方法的效果及不同物理配置下的可变形响应。论文还评估抓取任务成功与物体完整性，并通过脆弱物体操作的仿真到现实回放展示模拟物体的物理真实性。

items.title: RFW-S: Everyday Deformable Objects with Independent Simulation Verification

sections.text:
Household robots often need to operate appliances, and smart appliances offer both control panels and device APIs. Existing embodied AI simulation environments, however, model appliances solely as physical objects.

We introduce PAIR, a smart-home simulation environment grounded in the Matter protocol~\footnote{https://csa-iot.org/all-solutions/matter/}, the industry standard for smart-home devices. PAIR provides 84 smart-device assets whose functional control panels and APIs act on a shared device state, with ambient conditions that evolve in response to both.

From a survey of 1,443 requests, we construct a benchmark of 40 tasks that all require object manipulation yet remain solvable without API access, with 340 human demonstrations for policy training. Whether run alone, with a high-level planner, or with an API-enabled planner, two fine-tuned VLA policies complete none of the 120 evaluation episodes.

Robots rarely get far enough to use the API: even with oracle plans and API access, over 90\% of failed rollouts stall at navigating, grasping, or operating a door. With a perfect oracle in place of the robot's body, the best planner still gets through only 57.3\% of its plan.

When choosing between pressing a button and calling an API, several planners go by whether they can read the panel, not by API latency.\footnote{We will release our code and data upon publication.}

summary.en: The paper presents PAIR, a Matter-based smart-home simulation environment where device control panels and APIs affect shared device states, alongside changing ambient conditions. Its benchmark contains tasks requiring object manipulation that remain solvable without API access, with human demonstrations for policy training. The authors report that two fine-tuned vision-language-action policies completed none of the evaluation episodes. Even with oracle plans and API access, most failed rollouts stalled at navigation, grasping, or door operation; a perfect oracle body still left the best planner completing only part of its plan.
summary.zh: 论文提出 PAIR，一个以 Matter 协议为基础的智能家居仿真环境，其中智能设备的实体控制面板与 API 作用于共享设备状态，环境条件也会随之变化。作者根据请求调查构建了包含 40 项任务的基准；每项任务都需要物体操作，但无需 API 也可完成，并提供人工示范用于策略训练。两种微调后的视觉语言动作策略在 120 个评估回合中均未完成任务。作者称，即使提供预言机计划和 API，超过九成失败回合仍卡在导航、抓取或开门；以完美预言机替代机器人身体时，最佳规划器也只完成其计划的 57.3%。若在按键和调用 API 之间选择，若干规划器依据是否能读懂面板，而非 API 延迟作决定。

items.title: PAIR: Bringing Household Robots into the Smart Home

sections.text:
Human data can support robot policy pretraining, but gains attributed to a data recipe may also reflect subset size, training variability, or downstream adaptation.

In an HPT implementation on a 20-task MetaWorld suite with three training blocks, a constrained random 5,000-recording subset matches most of the task-informed subset's gain over the 40,000-recording pool at 20,000 updates (3.69 of 4.29 percentage points), leaving equal-size selection differences of 0.60 points at 5,000 recordings and 0.45 points at 1,250 recordings, with wide paired intervals.

Across 12 comparisons, task orderings repeat across seeds for several contrasts, but a fixed predictor built from the other two seeds trails the mean or difficulty reference in at least one held-out fold for every comparison.

Neither mechanism probe shows its predicted positive interaction: task-slot mismatch yields an interaction of $-0.0347$ points after adaptation, and in a six-task observation experiment the observation-by-pretraining interaction changes sign between seeds ($-18.29$ and $+1.04$ points) while full-state pretraining gains are positive in both ($+6.37$ and $+2.31$ points).

This retrospective study shows how equal-size and capacity controls, seed-level reporting, and targeted interventions change the interpretation of apparent transfer gains.

summary.en: This retrospective study examines whether human-data pretraining gains for robot policies reflect data selection, subset size, training variability, or downstream adaptation. In an HPT implementation on MetaWorld, a constrained random subset reproduced most of the task-informed subset’s gain over the full pool, while equal-size selection differences were small and had wide paired intervals. Some task orderings repeated across seeds, but a fixed predictor lagged a reference in at least one held-out fold for every comparison. Neither mechanism probe showed its predicted positive interaction.
summary.zh: 本文回顾人类数据用于机器人策略预训练时，所谓迁移收益可能来自数据选择，也可能受子集规模、训练随机性和下游适配影响。作者在 MetaWorld 任务和多个训练种子上的分析显示，受限随机子集已复现任务信息子集相对完整数据池大部分收益，而等规模选择差异较小且区间较宽。任务排序虽有部分重复性，固定预测器在每项比较的至少一个留出折中仍落后于参考。两项机制探测均未出现预期的正向交互。

sections.text:
Autonomy development for marine autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs) remains challenging because field testing is costly and difficult to reproduce. Existing marine simulation tools provide mature capabilities in vessel dynamics, robotics integration, and visual rendering, but these strengths are emphasized differently across platforms.

This paper presents ASTRA, an ASV simulation framework built in NVIDIA Isaac Sim that combines marine vehicle dynamics, photorealistic perception, and Robot Operating System (ROS 2) autonomy interfaces within a common environment.

ASTRA incorporates a Fossen-style marine dynamics model together with geometry-based buoyancy and programmable spectral wave disturbances, enabling non-planar hydrostatic and wave-induced motion. The simulator reproduces the sensor configuration of a physical BlueBoat testbed, including GPS, IMU, LiDAR, and RGB-D sensing exposed through ROS 2.

This allows localization, perception, planning, and control software to be developed against interfaces consistent with the physical platform. The BlueBoat's existing ROS 2 localization and perception modules were ported directly into ASTRA, while targeted zero-propulsion experiments were used to verify the implemented wave-body coupling.

The simulated roll response was consistent with the expected non-oscillatory hydrostatic behavior, and heave remained highly coherent with the generated wave field, with approximately unity gain at the dominant wave frequency in the tested sea states.

ASTRA is intended as an open-source testbed for marine autonomy development, simulation-based benchmarking, and sim-to-real experimentation.

summary.en: The paper presents ASTRA, an ASV simulation framework built in NVIDIA Isaac Sim that combines marine dynamics, photorealistic perception, and ROS 2 autonomy interfaces. It uses a Fossen-style dynamics model, geometry-based buoyancy, and programmable spectral wave disturbances, and reproduces the sensor configuration of a physical BlueBoat testbed. Existing BlueBoat localization and perception modules were ported to the simulator. Targeted zero-propulsion experiments were used to verify wave-body coupling; in tested sea states, roll and heave responses were consistent with the described expected behavior.
summary.zh: 本文介绍 ASTRA，这是基于 NVIDIA Isaac Sim 的海上自主水面艇仿真框架，整合船舶动力学、逼真感知和 ROS 2 自主系统接口。框架采用 Fossen 风格动力学模型、几何浮力及可编程谱波扰动，并复现 BlueBoat 测试平台的 GPS、IMU、LiDAR 和 RGB-D 传感器配置。作者将现有定位与感知模块移植到仿真器，并以特定无推进实验验证波浪与船体耦合；测试中的横摇和升沉响应符合所述预期。

sections.text:
Existing agentic manipulation systems treat pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policies as opaque, language-only primitives: when a policy call fails under unfamiliar instructions or scene perturbations, the agent cannot steer its behavior and is forced into futile retries or costly manual takeover.

We present InteractVLA, a framework that turns pretrained flow-based VLAs into geometrically steerable and inspectable tools through a bidirectional geometric interface with vision-language agents.

In the forward direction, test-time geometric guidance translates an agent-specified end-effector target into input gradients through the action expert via a differentiable command-to-pose mapping, while soft-time target alignment treats arrival time as a latent execution index to match the target pose without distorting the policy's approach motion.

In the reverse direction, action-informed agentic refinement exposes generated action chunks and calibrated camera reprojections back to the agent, allowing it to diagnose spatial discrepancies, revise targets for subsequent VLA calls, or locally adjust motion segments on top of the guided trajectory.

Making the VLA controllable not only boosts online agentic tool use, but also unlocks effective recursive self-improvement (RSI), achieving state-of-the-art performance of 99.4\% on LIBERO-Plus, 48.62\% on RoboDojo, and 89.4\% on RoboCasa365.Project page: https://lingwupro.github.io/InteractVLA/.

summary.en: InteractVLA makes pretrained flow-based vision-language-action policies geometrically steerable and inspectable through a bidirectional interface with vision-language agents. Geometric guidance translates an agent-specified end-effector target into gradients through the action expert, while soft-time alignment matches the target pose. In the reverse direction, action chunks and calibrated camera reprojections are exposed to the agent to diagnose spatial discrepancies, revise targets, or locally adjust motion. The authors report improved online tool use, recursive self-improvement, and results on three manipulation benchmarks.
summary.zh: InteractVLA 将预训练的基于流的视觉—语言—动作策略转化为可通过几何信息引导和检查的工具。前向接口把智能体指定的末端执行器目标转为动作专家的输入梯度，并以软时间目标对齐匹配目标姿态；反向接口则向智能体展示动作片段及相机重投影，帮助诊断空间偏差、调整后续目标或局部修正动作。作者称该框架提升在线智能体工具使用，并支持递归自我改进；摘要报告了其在三个操作基准上的表现。

sections.text:
World action models (WAMs) introduce predictive supervision into robot policy learning by jointly modeling future visual observations and actions. Pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policies acquire rich visual and semantic representations as well as action-generation capabilities.

Their action objectives typically lack direct supervision for predicting future visual observations. Future videos in robot demonstrations record object motion and task progress. They can provide temporal visual supervision that complements action labels.

We propose Training-Only Video Supervision, which introduces future-video prediction as an auxiliary objective for VLA fine-tuning. We condition a randomly initialized video-prediction expert on the VLA's shared vision-language features. The expert learns to predict future video latents from robot demonstrations.

The video prediction loss and the original action loss jointly update the shared vision-language backbone, providing additional temporal visual supervision. After training, we remove the video expert and its adapter. The fine-tuned VLA retains its original action-generation pathway at inference.

On the 50-task RoboTwin 2.0 benchmark, our method achieves 71.18% average success, compared with $\pi_{0.5}$ of 58.33%.In a matched evaluation on four real-world manipulation tasks, success increases from 42.50% to 61.25%.These results show that future visual modeling can serve as auxiliary training supervision for pretrained VLAs.

The fine-tuned action policy benefits from this supervision without retaining a video-prediction branch at deployment.

summary.en: The paper proposes Training-Only Video Supervision, using future-video prediction as an auxiliary objective when fine-tuning pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policies. A randomly initialized expert predicts future video latents from shared vision-language features; its loss and the action loss jointly update the shared backbone. The expert and adapter are removed after training, leaving the original action pathway for inference. The authors report 71.18% average success on 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, versus 58.33% for π0.5, and an increase from 42.50% to 61.25% on four matched real-world manipulation tasks.
summary.zh: 论文提出“仅训练阶段的视频监督”，将未来视频预测作为预训练视觉—语言—动作（VLA）策略微调时的辅助目标。随机初始化的视频预测专家根据共享视觉—语言特征预测机器人演示中的未来视频潜变量，视频损失与动作损失共同更新共享骨干网络；训练后移除专家及适配器，推理时保留原动作生成路径。在RoboTwin 2.0的50项任务上，平均成功率为71.18%，基线π0.5为58.33%；四项真实操作任务的匹配评测中，成功率由42.50%升至61.25%。

sections.text:
JEPA-style latent world models let embodied agents plan toward new goals with model predictive control, but they are still too slow for real-life embodied control: sampling-based MPC repeats predictor inference tens of thousands of times per plan, and even on high-end GPUs one planning step can take tens of seconds.

We observe substantial latent locality in this repeated-inference workload: the predictor maps close actions to close latents, and inside a quantized predictor this closeness takes a form that hardware can exploit, differential bit-level sparsity.

Unlike an input stream, whose temporal similarity is given, a planner itself decides which candidates it evaluates together, so the planner can choose its own references and, with reference forest sampling, manufacture more sparsity: it couples the sampled action sequences of each group to a shared root, with competitive planning quality.

We build the accelerator on the insights of the rich line of bit-level sparsity accelerators and design it and the planner tightly coupled as a single co-design: the planner increases sparsity and exposes structure for hardware scheduling, and the bit-exact hardware effectively uses the sparsity that the planner creates.

On three JEPA world models, our co-design is 1.28-1.80x faster than a dense accelerator and uses 38-52% less energy, and it is 1.22-1.58x faster than prior bit-sparse design and uses 16-36% less energy, with the same area.

summary.en: The paper presents a planner-hardware co-design to reduce the cost of sampling-based model predictive control with JEPA-style latent world models. Across three JEPA world models, the co-design is reported to be 1.28–1.80 times faster and use 38–52% less energy than a dense accelerator. Compared with a prior bit-sparse design, it is 1.22–1.58 times faster and uses 16–36% less energy at the same area.

sections.text:
Reliable localization in long underground infrastructures remains a major challenge for autonomous inspection robots. In hydropower spillway tunnels and drainage galleries, repetitive geometric structures provide insufficient constraints along the tunnel axis, while weak texture and illumination variations further degrade visual estimation.

Under this coupled degradation, existing LiDAR-inertial and visual-inertial odometry systems may lose the ability to recover continuous longitudinal motion. This paper presents DGV-DLIVO, a degeneracy-guided visual fusion for direct LiDAR-inertial-visual odometry for extreme tunnel environments.

Instead of treating vision as a general complementary sensor, the proposed method exploits the LiDAR-degenerate direction as an active guidance signal to determine informative visual regions, establish LiDAR-anchored visual associations, and perform subspace-selective fusion.

The visual constraints are introduced only into the deficient motion subspace, while unreliable LiDAR information in the same direction is adaptively suppressed and reliable geometric constraints are preserved.

Real-world experiments in hydropower tunnels demonstrate that representative state-of-the-art LIO, LIVO, and VIO methods suffer from stagnation, oscillation, severe under-travel, curved drift, or divergence, whereas DGV-DLIVO maintains continuous and directionally consistent tunnel-axis motion estimation under both cart-mounted and handheld acquisition.

It achieves a 91.4% progress ratio over the 40m tunnel sequence and significantly improves longitudinal recovery and trajectory stability. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of degeneracy-guided adaptive fusion for robotic inspection in severely degraded underground environments.

The source code and a supplementary video are publicly available at https://github.com/0RayZhang0/DGV-DLIVO.

summary.en: The paper presents DGV-DLIVO, which uses the LiDAR-degenerate direction to guide visual-region selection, establish LiDAR-anchored visual associations, and fuse visual constraints selectively in the deficient motion subspace while suppressing unreliable LiDAR information there. In real-world hydropower-tunnel experiments, the authors report continuous, directionally consistent tunnel-axis motion estimates for both cart-mounted and handheld acquisition. The method achieves a 91.4% progress ratio on a 40-meter tunnel sequence.

sections.text:
This paper examines why distributed optimization degrades when multi-robot systems coordinate under realistic communication delays.

Using consensus ADMM as a representative framework for generating collision-free, dynamically feasible motion plans in both trajectory optimization and receding-horizon control settings, we show that delay degrades performance structurally: the consensus and dual updates weight stale and current information identically, so staleness enters the optimizer disguised as genuine disagreement and accumulates through the multipliers.

Delay-agnostic adaptation (e.g. residual balancing) inherits this contamination and can perform worse than a fixed penalty.

We introduce a Delay-Aware ADMM (DA-ADMM) variant that adapts penalty parameters to real-time delay statistics and re-derives the global consensus update as a delay-weighted average, down-weighting stale information in favor of recent updates.

Simulations in 2D and 3D show that DA-ADMM improves robustness, success rate, and solution quality over fixed-parameter, residual-balancing, lower-bound, and fixed-constraint baselines. Degradation is therefore governed not by delay length or frequency, but by the optimizer's ability to reason over the age of the information it receives.

summary.en: The paper analyzes how communication delays affect consensus ADMM for distributed multi-robot motion planning: consensus and dual updates treat stale and current information equally, allowing staleness to appear as disagreement and accumulate in the multipliers. The authors introduce DA-ADMM, which adapts penalty parameters using real-time delay statistics and weights the global consensus update toward more recent information. Simulations in 2D and 3D report improved robustness, success rate, and solution quality over several specified baselines.
summary.zh: 论文分析共识 ADMM 在通信延迟下用于多机器人运动规划时的退化机制：共识和对偶更新同等处理新旧信息，使陈旧信息被当作真实分歧并累积到乘子中，延迟无关的残差平衡可能因此不如固定惩罚参数。作者提出 DA-ADMM，根据实时延迟统计调整惩罚参数，并以延迟加权共识更新降低陈旧信息权重。二维和三维仿真显示，该方法相较多种基线提高了鲁棒性、成功率和解质量。

sections.text:
Recent world action models (WAMs) drop future prediction at inference, assuming that representations learned through auxiliary future supervision still benefit action generation.

However, our layerwise analysis of Fast-WAM reveals a depth-dependent mismatch: while probes decode future state transitions more accurately from deeper visual layers, the gradients and visual focuses of the future and action objectives increasingly diverge with depth, leaving much of this predictive information unused by the action pathway.

To address this issue, we introduce RelayWAM, which adds an explicit transition space between the video and action backbones.

Conditioned on the task instruction, robot state, and current action estimate, recurrent transition layers extract step-relevant predictive cues across depth and relay them directly into the action attention, without generating future frames at inference.

Experiments show that RelayWAM substantially amplifies the benefit of future supervision, translating into stronger generalization under distribution shifts in both simulation and real-world robot tasks. On LIBERO-Plus, RelayWAM achieves 72.03% mean success, compared to 56.42% without future supervision and 51.50% for Fast-WAM.

summary.en: The paper reports that deeper Fast-WAM visual layers encode future state transitions more accurately, while the gradients and visual focus of future-prediction and action objectives diverge with depth, leaving predictive information underused. It introduces RelayWAM, an explicit transition space between video and action backbones that relays task-relevant predictive cues into action attention without generating future frames at inference. Experiments report stronger generalization under distribution shifts in simulation and real-world robot tasks; on LIBERO-Plus, mean success is 72.03%.
summary.zh: 论文指出，Fast-WAM 深层视觉表示虽更易解码未来状态转移，但未来预测目标与动作目标的梯度和视觉关注随深度增加而分化，使预测信息未充分用于动作生成。为此，作者提出 RelayWAM，在视频与动作骨干之间加入显式转移空间，以任务指令、机器人状态和当前动作估计为条件提取预测线索并传入动作注意力，推理时不生成未来帧。作者报告其在仿真和真实机器人任务的分布变化下泛化更强；在 LIBERO-Plus 上平均成功率为72.03%。

sections.text:
Vision-language-action (VLA) policies incur control stalls when inference blocks the next action chunk. Asynchronous early inference can hide latency, but its results may be inconsistent with the arriving actual inputs. Unconditional reuse risks acting on mismatched inputs, whereas full recomputation discards useful precomputation.

We propose SR-VLA, combining predicted-input lookahead with selective KV cache repair. During current chunk execution, a lightweight action-conditioned predictor generates next-boundary visual observations and proprioceptive state.

These predictions, together with the task instruction, drive the frozen VLA to precompute a speculative KV cache and action chunk. After real inputs are available to VLA, predicted--real differences and task conditions determine whether to accept the action chunk or trigger selective KV repair.

On LIBERO, SR-VLA achieves $2.67\times$ and $1.27\times$ query speedups over the respective synchronous $\pi_{0.5}$ and OpenVLA-OFT baselines, while maintaining competitive average task success rates. Under target-motion perturbation, success remains baseline-comparable, with $1.52\times$--$1.93\times$ query speedup.

summary.en: The paper proposes SR-VLA, which uses an action-conditioned predictor during execution of the current action chunk to estimate the next-boundary visual observations and proprioceptive state. A frozen VLA uses these predictions to precompute a KV cache and action chunk; when actual inputs arrive, their differences and task conditions determine whether to accept the chunk or selectively repair the cache. On LIBERO, the authors report query speedups of 2.67× over synchronous π0.5 and 1.27× over OpenVLA-OFT, with competitive average task success. Under target-motion perturbation, success remains comparable to baseline.
summary.zh: 论文提出 SR-VLA，以动作条件预测器在当前动作块执行期间预测下一边界的视觉观测和本体状态，并据此让冻结的 VLA 预先计算 KV 缓存和动作块。真实输入到达后，系统依据预测与实际输入的差异及任务条件，决定接受动作块或进行选择性 KV 缓存修复。在 LIBERO 上，作者报告相较同步 π0.5 和 OpenVLA-OFT 的查询速度分别提升2.67倍和1.27倍，同时保持有竞争力的平均任务成功率；目标运动扰动下也报告了基线相当的成功率。

sections.text:
Generalised referring expression comprehension (GREC) aims to identify and localise the zero, one or multiple objects referred to by a language expression. In robotic manipulation, grounding also needs to remain accurate when requests for the same objects are paraphrased or embedded in additional context in robotics.

However, grounding expert models are sensitive to instruction variation, while generative vision--language models (VLMs) struggle with complete target recovery and rejection of absent targets. These complementary limitations motivate combining the contextual representations of VLMs with the direct spatial prediction capabilities of grounding experts.

We therefore introduce VLM-guided Grounding Expert (VGE), which combines a frozen VLM with a trainable grounding expert through layerwise joint attention and text-conditioned instance scoring. These interfaces leverage multimodal understanding of the VLM to guide object-query refinement and candidate selection while retaining direct bounding-box prediction.

Across three datasets, VGE achieves the highest averaged F1 score among the evaluated methods on all five test splits, with differences of at most 1.2 percentage points across instruction conditions within each split.

On the dataset with robotic scenes, VGE also achieves the highest F1 across instruction variants and no-target, single-target and multiple-target cases. VGE provides a $5.3$--$13.0\times$ inference speedup over the baseline with the same VLM base model.

These results support combining VLM context with specialised spatial prediction to address both grounding challenges, with particularly strong performance in robotic scenes. Code will be released upon publication.

summary.en: The paper introduces VLM-guided Grounding Expert (VGE), combining a frozen vision-language model with a trainable grounding expert through layerwise joint attention and text-conditioned instance scoring. The authors report the highest average F1 among evaluated methods on five test splits across three datasets, with at most 1.2 percentage points of variation across instruction conditions within a split. On robotic scenes, it also leads across instruction variants and target counts, and is 5.3–13.0 times faster than a baseline using the same VLM base model.

sections.text:
ARC 1 introduced a three-layer governance architecture for autonomous systems comprising model safety validation, cognitive certification (CRAB), and operational authorization (LEA).However, it did not address how compliance should be maintained after deployment.

This paper introduces Delta Management, a continuous governance framework that measures deviations between a system's current operational state and its certified baseline, defined as a region rather than a fixed point. Compliance is assessed through continuous monitoring instead of static certification. Four extensions are proposed.

First, CRAB evaluation incorporates the worst verified behavioral deviations, with isolated outliers quarantined pending confirmation to prevent unjustified restrictions.

Second, a layered trigger taxonomy distinguishes hard safety violations, critical single-dimension failures, correlated multi-system degradation, and risk-weighted composite indicators, each triggering proportionate responses.

Third, a graduated safe transition protocol separates withdrawal of operational authorization from physical shutdown, consistent with established safety standards and EU AI Act requirements.

Fourth, environmental delta is introduced as a distinct baseline validity condition: environmental drift beyond the certified Operational Design Domain (ODD) triggers recertification or ODD revision rather than automatic authority contraction.

Together, these extensions transform ARC from a deployment-time certification architecture into a continuous framework for monitoring, evaluating, and enforcing compliance throughout the operational lifecycle of autonomous systems. The framework addresses the continuous compliance obligations established by EU AI Act Article 72（2）.

summary.en: The paper presents Delta Management, a framework intended to extend autonomous-system governance from deployment-time certification to continuous compliance monitoring. It compares current operations with a certified baseline defined as a region, and proposes four extensions: evaluating the worst verified behavioral deviations, using tiered triggers for proportionate responses, separating withdrawal of operational authorization from physical shutdown, and treating environmental drift as a baseline-validity condition. Drift beyond the certified operational design domain prompts recertification or domain revision. The authors say the framework addresses continuous compliance obligations in Article 72(2) of the EU AI Act.
summary.zh: 论文提出Delta Management，旨在将自主系统治理从部署时认证延伸到运行全生命周期的持续合规监测。框架将当前运行状态与作为区域而非固定点的认证基线比较，并提出四项扩展：纳入最严重且经核实的行为偏差、按风险类型分层触发响应、区分撤销运行授权与物理关机，以及将环境变化作为基线有效性条件。若环境漂移超出认证的运行设计域，则触发重新认证或修订该域，而非自动收缩权限。作者称该框架回应了欧盟《人工智能法案》第72条第2款的持续合规要求。

sections.text:
Physical agents must use what they previously saw or touched after visibility or contact is lost. Their actions change the implications of these remembered facts. We introduce executable perceptual memory (EPM), a world-model framework that advances explicit perceptual state alongside neural latent dynamics during imagination.

Its evolving read-out informs reward prediction, value estimation and policy learning. We align reward inputs with the transitions that produced them and supervise the reward head on open-loop rollouts of recorded actions.

On Memory Maze $13\times13$, EPM reaches 30.37 return at 1M interactions, compared with 23.37 when the same evolving read-out informs only policy and value on a common perceptual front end: a gain of 7.00 [3.80, 10.21].The complete method also improves control on $9\times9$ and in MiniWorld.

Probes of remembered, out-of-view arrivals show stronger reward anticipation in both visual implementations. Concentration, tactile recovery and real tactile frames demonstrate complementary roles of remembered facts in imagined-policy training, motion-dependent decisions and sensory-content retention.

EPM connects persistent perception to the predicted consequences and learning signals of a world model for Physical AI.

summary.en: The paper introduces executable perceptual memory (EPM), which advances an explicit perceptual state alongside neural latent dynamics during world-model imagination. Its evolving read-out informs reward prediction, value estimation, and policy learning; reward inputs are aligned with the transitions that produced them. On Memory Maze 13×13 at one million interactions, the authors report a return of 30.37, versus 23.37 when the same read-out informs only policy and value on a common perceptual front end. They also report improved control on 9×9 and MiniWorld, and describe complementary memory roles in probes and tactile experiments.
summary.zh: 论文提出可执行感知记忆（EPM），在世界模型想象过程中推进显式感知状态与神经潜在动态，使记忆信息参与奖励预测、价值估计和策略学习。方法将奖励输入与产生它的状态转移对齐，并在记录动作的开放环路轨迹上监督奖励头。在Memory Maze 13×13、100万次交互时，作者报告EPM回报为30.37；同一感知前端下，仅让演化读出参与策略和价值的对照为23.37，差值7.00。完整方法还在9×9和MiniWorld改善控制；探测及触觉实验显示记忆对奖励预期、运动决策和感官内容保留有不同作用。

sections.text:
Decoupled multi-robot motion planning avoids the high-dimensional joint configuration space but requires repeated single-robot planning among moving obstacles, where route choice and timing are coupled. We develop a framework based on graphs of space-time convex sets (ST-GCSs) for continuous spatiotemporal planning and multi-robot coordination.

An ST-GCS represents collision-free space-time by convex sets, allowing the sequence of regions and the geometry and timing of piecewise-linear trajectories to be optimized jointly under velocity limits.

To incorporate moving obstacles and previously planned robots, we develop Exact Convex Decomposition (ECD), which removes their swept occupancies while maintaining a convex decomposition for subsequent planning queries.

Building on path-based GCS search, we develop a best-first solver tailored to the ST-GCS motion model, exploiting temporal reachability for dominance pruning and using admissible heuristics with separate or joint search-key evaluation. Precomputed heuristic bounds can also be reused across reservation-updated graphs.

We integrate ST-GCS planning and ECD into prioritized multi-robot planning and introduce windowed coordination with dynamic window adjustment to limit reservation-induced graph growth.

Experiments demonstrate improved scalability and competitive solution quality against optimization-based and sampling-based planners on challenging spatiotemporal and multi-robot problems. Large-scale simulations coordinate up to $100$ robots within a minute, while real-robot demonstrations showcase the practical applicability of the framework.

Project homepage: https://sites.google.com/view/stgcs.

summary.en: The paper develops a framework for continuous spatiotemporal motion planning and multi-robot coordination using graphs of space-time convex sets (ST-GCSs). It represents collision-free space-time with convex regions and jointly optimizes region sequences and piecewise-linear trajectory geometry and timing under velocity limits. Exact Convex Decomposition removes swept occupancy from moving obstacles and planned robots. A tailored best-first solver and windowed coordination are also introduced. Experiments report improved scalability and competitive solution quality; large-scale simulations coordinate up to 100 robots within a minute, and real-robot demonstrations are presented.
summary.zh: 论文提出基于时空凸集图（ST-GCS）的连续时空运动规划与多机器人协调框架，将无碰撞时空表示为凸集，并联合优化区域序列及分段线性轨迹的几何和时间，同时满足速度限制。为处理移动障碍物及已规划机器人，作者提出精确凸分解以移除其扫掠占用；还设计利用时间可达性剪枝和可采纳启发式的优先搜索求解器，并结合优先级规划与动态调整窗口的协调方法。实验显示该方法在复杂问题上具备可扩展性和有竞争力的解质量；大规模仿真中一分钟内协调最多100台机器人，另有真实机器人演示。

sections.text:
Industrial manipulation requires precise alignment and controlled handling of rigid, deformable, and flexible components. Yet, the benefits of pretrained visuomotor policies remain underexplored in settings where limited access to specialized hardware, components, and fixtures constrains demonstration collection and evaluation.

Understanding task-specific data requirements is important for assessing their scalability across diverse processes on the factory floor. We investigate whether video pretraining can support reliable industrial manipulation with limited action data.

We propose FLUX-mimic, a video-action model, motivated by the potential of video pretraining to capture motion and interaction patterns that enable sample-efficient training. FLUX-mimic is built on a backbone pretrained on large-scale web and industrial task data, and an action expert to generate robot trajectories.

We train our policy by joint video-action training. Across four automotive manufacturing benchmark tasks and two bimanual robot platforms, FLUX-mimic outperforms all considered baselines on the dexterous robot platform and matches pi_{0.5}'s average success rate on the gripper-based robot platform.

On a deformable part kitting task, FLUX-mimic reaches 77.5% success with as little as two hours of task-specific action-labeled demonstrations.

summary.en: The paper investigates whether video pretraining can support industrial manipulation when action-labeled demonstrations are limited, and proposes FLUX-mimic, a video-action model with a pretrained backbone and an action expert for generating robot trajectories. It is trained jointly on video and action data. Across four automotive manufacturing benchmark tasks and two bimanual robot platforms, the authors report that it outperforms considered baselines on the dexterous platform and matches π₀.₅'s average success rate on the gripper-based platform.

sections.text:
Human demonstrations offer an efficient and scalable source of data for dexterous robot manipulation, but differences in sensing and hand morphology complicate the transfer of contact-rich interactions. We present TouchBridge, a hardware--software co-designed framework for human-to-robot data transformation.

A wearable human demonstration interface and a corresponding robot interface establish cross-embodiment correspondence in visual and fingertip tactile sensing. We introduce Tac-Retarget, a tactile-conditioned retargeting method that uses measured contact to align fingertip contact patches and preserve their spatial relations within and across hands.

Unlike object-aware or simulation-based transfer pipelines, Tac-Retarget requires no object mesh, object-pose estimate, or physics simulation for retargeting, enabling direct and scalable conversion of human demonstrations into robot-domain training data.

Combined with visual synthesis and camera-anchored action conversion, TouchBridge produces robot-domain demonstrations for fine-tuning a pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) model.

Across four real-world contact-rich tasks, policies fine-tuned solely on TouchBridge-converted human demonstrations achieve a 72.5% average success rate, compared with 77.5% using an equal number of teleoperated robot demonstrations, while human demonstration collection is 7.0x faster.

Under the same policy and training setup, Tac-Retarget outperforms DexPilot and UniDex by 25.0 and 42.5 percentage points, respectively.

summary.en: TouchBridge is a hardware and software framework for converting human demonstrations into robot-domain training data. Its Tac-Retarget method uses measured tactile contact to align fingertip contact patches and their spatial relations, without requiring object meshes, pose estimates, or physics simulation. Combined with visual synthesis and camera-anchored action conversion, it supports fine-tuning a pretrained vision-language-action model. Across four real-world contact-rich tasks, policies trained only on converted demonstrations achieved a 72.5% average success rate, versus 77.5% with an equal number of teleoperated robot demonstrations; collection was 7.0 times faster.
summary.zh: 论文提出 TouchBridge，通过可穿戴人类演示接口与机器人接口建立视觉和指尖触觉对应，并以 Tac-Retarget 根据实测接触对齐指尖接触区域及其空间关系。该方法无需物体网格、物体位姿估计或物理仿真进行重定向；结合视觉合成和相机锚定动作转换，可生成用于微调预训练视觉语言动作模型的机器人域演示。四项真实世界接触丰富任务中，相关策略平均成功率为 72.5%，同量遥操作机器人演示为 77.5%；人类演示采集快 7 倍。

sections.text:
Underwater visual systems often suffer from blurry textures and low color contrast due to the inevitable light propagation. These issues can significantly degrade the perception of stable robotic operations.

In this paper, we introduce a novel learning-based sensing system that tackles the multidimensional vision tasks in underwater; concretely, we deal with image enhancement, depth estimation, and uncertainty for 3-D visual systems.

Also, we propose a TRIDENT model in a fast and lightweight manner; TRIDENT consists of three parallelized decoders and one backbone structure for efficient feature sharing. In addition, it is designed to be trained to express complex parameterization.

In experimental evaluation on several standard datasets, we demonstrate that TRIDENT significantly outperforms other existing methods on image enhancement and depth estimation. Despite performing three tasks, our model has better efficiency than the others for both memory size and inference time.

Finally, our joint learning approach demonstrates robustness in feature matching and seamlessly extends from 2-D to 3-D vision tasks. Supplements are available at https://sites.google.com/view/underwater-trident/home

summary.en: The paper introduces TRIDENT, a learning-based system for underwater robot vision that jointly handles image enhancement, depth estimation, and uncertainty. Its architecture uses one backbone for feature sharing and three parallel decoders. Experiments on several standard datasets are reported to show better image enhancement and depth estimation than existing methods, along with improved memory and inference-time efficiency despite the three tasks. The authors also report robustness in feature matching and an extension of the joint learning approach from 2D to 3D vision tasks.
summary.zh: 论文提出 TRIDENT，一种面向水下三维机器人视觉感知的联合学习系统，处理图像增强、深度估计和不确定性任务。模型采用共享骨干网络与三个并行解码器，以共享特征并兼顾效率。作者称，在若干标准数据集的实验中，TRIDENT 在图像增强和深度估计方面优于现有方法，尽管执行三项任务，其内存占用和推理时间效率也更好；联合学习还表现出特征匹配鲁棒性，并可从二维视觉扩展至三维视觉任务。

sections.text:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models integrate visual perception, language understanding, and action generation to control robots. Testing these systems produces trajectories and task outcomes, but existing approaches provide limited guidance on using these recorded trajectories to assess subsequent executions or inform policy repair.

We conjecture that, for a given policy and task, traversing certain workspace regions is associated with a higher likelihood of failure. To investigate this conjecture, we propose VoxelSBFL, a black-box adaptation of Spectrum-Based Fault Localization (SBFL) in which workspace voxels replace program elements as units of analysis.

Recorded tool-center-point (TCP) trajectories provide binary voxel coverage, which is combined with execution outcomes to construct suspiciousness maps using established SBFL formulas. These maps identify failure-associated regions and score unseen trajectories without requiring internal model access.

We evaluate 34 spectrum-based techniques across four VLA models using 96,000 Pick-Up trajectories in simulation and compare the leading techniques against eight action- and trajectory-based metrics. VoxelSBFL obtains an overall macro ROC-AUC of 0.704, significantly outperforming state-of-the art baselines.

Sensitivity analyses show that performance varies with spatial granularity and training-set size. These findings support spatial spectra for VLA execution assessment and motivate future research on runtime monitoring, self-healing and targeted policy improvement.

summary.en: The paper proposes VoxelSBFL, a black-box adaptation of spectrum-based fault localization for vision-language-action models. It treats workspace voxels as analysis units and combines binary voxel coverage from tool-center-point trajectories with execution outcomes to create suspiciousness maps. These maps mark failure-associated regions and score unseen trajectories without access to model internals. The authors evaluate 34 spectrum-based techniques across four models using simulated pickup trajectories and compare leading methods with eight action- and trajectory-based metrics. They report an overall macro ROC-AUC of 0.704 and better performance than the baselines. Sensitivity analyses indicate that results vary with spatial granularity and training-set size.
summary.zh: 本文提出 VoxelSBFL，将基于频谱的故障定位方法用于视觉—语言—动作模型：以工作空间体素代替程序元素，根据工具中心点轨迹的二元体素覆盖和执行结果生成可疑度图，用于识别与失败相关的区域并评估未见轨迹，无需访问模型内部。作者在四种模型的模拟环境中，使用抓取轨迹评估34种频谱技术，并与八种动作或轨迹指标比较；报告总体宏平均 ROC-AUC 为0.704，且优于基线。敏感性分析显示性能受空间粒度和训练集大小影响。

items.title: VoxelSBFL: Voxel-Level Spectrum-Based Failure Prediction for Vision-Language-Action Models

sections.text:
Diffusion models are increasingly adopted in robotics and control due to their capability to express multiple feasible solutions to a given task. However, the role of stochasticity in the diffusion model-sampler across denoising remains poorly understood.

We introduce a per-timestep counterfactual diagnostic that tests how changing the sampled noise affects the final output.

Across five model-sampler configurations spanning three robotics benchmarks, diverse architectures, domains, and conditioning mechanisms, we reveal highly varied temporal sensitivity profiles, where noise-induced deviations can amplify, partially contract, or undergo near-total attenuation downstream.

From these profiles, we define stochastic diversity windows (SDWs): compact intervals that identify where sampler stochasticity has the strongest measured influence on the final output.

Guided by these windows, we apply two heuristic interventions: targeted stochastic amplification, which increases sample diversity exploration of the solution space, and an SDW-hybrid sampler, which replaces DDPM steps with DDIM skips in low-impact regions, resulting in network evaluation reductions of up to 40-60% and wall-clock time by up to 85%, with no consistent changes detected in feasibility, cost, or diversity across held-out tasks.

summary.en: The paper introduces a per-timestep counterfactual diagnostic to test how changes in sampled noise affect diffusion model outputs, and defines stochastic diversity windows (SDWs) as compact intervals where stochasticity has its strongest measured influence. Across five model-sampler configurations spanning three robotics benchmarks, the authors observe that noise-induced deviations may amplify, partially contract, or nearly disappear downstream. They use the windows to guide targeted stochastic amplification and a hybrid sampler that replaces DDPM steps with DDIM skips in low-impact regions. The abstract reports up to 40–60% fewer network evaluations and up to 85% lower wall-clock time, with no consistent changes detected in feasibility, cost, or diversity across held-out tasks.
summary.zh: 本文提出逐时间步反事实诊断，检验扩散模型采样过程中改变噪声对最终输出的影响，并据此定义随机多样性窗口（SDW），标出采样随机性影响最强的紧凑区间。作者在涵盖三个机器人基准的五种模型—采样器配置中观察到，噪声引发的偏差可能放大、部分收缩或几乎完全衰减。基于窗口，作者尝试定向增强随机性，以及在低影响区用 DDIM 跳步替代 DDPM 步骤。摘要报告后者最多减少40%–60%的网络评估、最多缩短85%的运行时间；在留出任务中，未检测到可行性、成本或多样性的稳定变化。

sections.text:
Understanding requirements for systems involving humans and robots is essential for providing robust evidence that such systems behave correctly. Requirements formalisation approaches such as the Formal Requirements Elicitation Tool (FRET) can support the transition from unstructured natural language to formal representations suitable for verification.

In this paper, we formalise 146 hazard-derived natural-language requirements for a Robot-Assisted Dressing (RAD) case study, previously classified using a taxonomy of Human-Robot Teamwork (HRT) requirements. Through an iterative process involving domain-expert clarification, these were represented by 117 unique FRETISH requirements.

Formalisation exposed ambiguities, temporal and probabilistic assumptions, and cases where source requirements needed to be decomposed or could be consolidated because they expressed the same formal behaviour.

Temporal analysis showed that 70.1% of the unique FRETISH requirements use either immediate-response or ordering constraints (immediately or before), while formalisation also exposed relationships between requirements across HRT taxonomy categories. We further analyse the formal semantics and realisability of the resulting requirements.

The results show that HRT classification and formalisation provide complementary views: the taxonomy captures the teamwork concern represented by a requirement, while FRETISH makes the required behaviour explicit. We report practical lessons and limitations of applying FRET to HRT requirements and identify directions for further work.

summary.en: The paper formalizes 146 hazard-derived natural-language requirements for a robot-assisted dressing case study, producing 117 unique FRETISH requirements through iterative domain-expert clarification. The process revealed ambiguities, temporal and probabilistic assumptions, and requirements that needed decomposition or consolidation. Temporal analysis found that 70.1% of the unique requirements used immediate-response or ordering constraints. The authors argue that human-robot teamwork classification and FRETISH offer complementary views, and discuss practical lessons, limitations, and future directions.
summary.zh: 本文以机器人辅助穿衣案例研究，将146条由危害分析得出的自然语言需求形式化。经领域专家澄清和迭代，最终形成117条独特的FRETISH需求。形式化过程揭示了歧义、时间与概率假设，以及需要拆分或合并的需求。分析显示，70.1%的需求包含即时响应或先后顺序约束，并暴露了人机团队需求分类之间的联系。作者认为，分类与形式化分别呈现团队协作关注点和明确行为要求，并讨论了应用经验、局限及后续方向。

sections.text:
Collaboration promises to extend humanoid capabilities beyond what individual robots can achieve. However, realizing this potential requires coordinated whole-body interactions, coherent long-horizon planning, and precise synchronization across robots.

We introduce Heave-Ho, a decentralized framework for long-horizon collaborative multi-humanoid loco-manipulation. At the low level, we develop a multi-agent post-training framework that adapts a humanoid foundation tracking model to physically coupled interactions between humanoids, enabling coordinated decentralized control from local observations alone.

At the high level, we train a vision-language planner and design a speech-based leader-follower coordination mechanism to synchronize decentralized execution without network communication. Trained with two identical humanoids, our system scales to teams of up to ten robots and generalizes to heterogeneous teams without retraining.

To benchmark these capabilities, we introduce HH-Bench, comprising 12 tasks involving teams of 2 to 10 humanoids, including heterogeneous teams. Systematic evaluations show that Heave-Ho consistently outperforms baseline methods, while real-world experiments demonstrate robust decentralized collaboration across challenging tasks.

summary.en: The authors introduce Heave-Ho, a decentralized framework for long-horizon collaborative locomotion and manipulation by humanoid teams. Its low-level multi-agent post-training adapts a tracking model to physically coupled interactions, enabling control from local observations. A vision-language planner and speech-based leader-follower mechanism coordinate execution without network communication. Trained with two identical humanoids, the system is reported to scale to teams of up to ten and generalize to heterogeneous teams without retraining. Evaluations on the 12-task HH-Bench outperform baselines, and real-world experiments demonstrate collaboration on challenging tasks.
summary.zh: 本文提出Heave-Ho，一种用于多台人形机器人长期协作运动与操作的去中心化框架。低层方法通过多智能体后训练，使跟踪模型适应机器人间的物理耦合，并仅依据本地观测进行协同控制；高层结合视觉语言规划器与基于语音的主从协调机制，在无网络通信下同步执行。系统以两台相同机器人训练，作者报告其可扩展至最多十台机器人，并能推广到异构团队而无需重新训练。HH-Bench包含2至10台机器人的12项任务；系统评估优于基线，真实世界实验展示了具有挑战性任务中的协作表现。

The team trajectories for a cooperative task can be generated by a generative model, provided that the model has been trained on demonstrations of the agents cooperating. sections.text:
The agents in a heterogeneous team can cooperate to accomplish tasks that exceed their individual capabilities. The team trajectories for a cooperative task can be generated by a generative model, provided that the model has been trained on demonstrations of the agents cooperating.

Yet, demonstrations of cooperation are costly and may not exist for tasks that the team has never performed. The conditions under which the agents can combine their capabilities, however, are physical properties of the team and are known before any demonstration is collected.

We encode the conditions as constraints on the team trajectories, and we enforce the constraints while sampling from generative models trained on demonstrations of each agent alone. We prove that the proposed method can generate every team trajectory that satisfies the constraints, although the demonstrations contain no cooperation.

Hence the constraints determine which team trajectories can be generated, and the demonstrations determine how likely each team trajectory is. Numerical results on two cooperative tasks show the effectiveness of the method, which generates cooperative team trajectories that satisfy the constraints and requires no retraining when agents join or leave the team.

Finally, we implement the method on a multi-robot testbed.

summary.en: The paper addresses how heterogeneous agents can combine capabilities when cooperation demonstrations are unavailable. The method encodes known physical properties of the team as trajectory constraints and enforces them while sampling from generative models trained on demonstrations from individual agents. The authors prove that it can generate every team trajectory satisfying the constraints; constraints determine which trajectories are possible, while demonstrations determine their likelihood. Numerical results on two cooperative tasks show constraint-satisfying trajectories and no need for retraining when agents join or leave. The method is also implemented on a multi-robot testbed.
summary.zh: 本文研究如何让异构团队在缺少协作示范时组合各自能力。方法将已知的团队物理条件编码为轨迹约束，并在仅用各个智能体单独示范训练的生成模型中采样时施加这些约束。作者证明，该方法能够生成所有满足约束的团队轨迹：约束决定可生成的轨迹，示范则决定其可能性。两个协作任务的数值结果显示，生成轨迹满足约束，且团队成员加入或退出时无需重新训练。作者还在多机器人测试平台上实现了该方法。

sections.text:
Making automated vehicles accessible requires consideration of vulnerable road users, including wheelchair users. To offer a more tailored experience that supports independence for this group, vehicle design needs to accommodate the wide range of wheelchair configurations.

However, wheelchairs are individualized, varying in frame geometry, propulsion, and visual appearance. Moreover, occupants or accessories may obscure visual cues. Existing mobility-aid datasets only label the presence of a wheelchair, rather than describing its specific configuration.

To fill this gap, this paper introduces the Wheelchair Configuration Image Dataset (WCID), comprising 467 face-blurred images across 192 capture groups solely for evaluation.

Each image is annotated with (i) a two-class label of manual or powered, (ii) a chair subtype, (iii) occupancy, viewpoint, setting, lighting, occlusion, propulsion, and control, with a 273-image validation split and 194-image test split.

Three convolutional neural network backbones and a frozen vision-language probe are trained on an external image dataset and evaluated on WCID to measure cross-dataset generalization, while also testing robustness using Gaussian blur. Convolutional models do well on clean images, but performance drops under strong blur, leaving a gap before deployment.

Code, split assignments, labels, trained weights, and the face-blurred images is available at: https://github.com/Mi3-Lab/MAID

summary.en: The paper introduces the Wheelchair Configuration Image Dataset (WCID) to evaluate recognition of wheelchair configurations. It contains 467 face-blurred images annotated for manual or powered type, chair subtype, occupancy, viewpoint, setting, lighting, occlusion, propulsion, and controls. The study trains three convolutional neural network backbones and a frozen vision-language probe on an external image dataset, then evaluates cross-dataset generalization and robustness to Gaussian blur. The authors report that convolutional models perform well on clean images, but performance falls under strong blur, leaving a gap before deployment.
summary.zh: 论文介绍轮椅配置图像数据集 WCID，用于评估模型识别轮椅具体配置的能力。数据集含 467 张人脸模糊图像，并标注手动或电动类别、轮椅子类型及占用、视角、环境、光照、遮挡、驱动方式和控制装置等信息。研究以外部图像数据集训练三种卷积神经网络和一种冻结的视觉语言探针，再测试跨数据集泛化及高斯模糊鲁棒性。作者报告卷积模型在清晰图像上表现良好，但强模糊会导致性能下降，距离部署仍有差距。

As real-robot data collection scales, collection-system design shapes both operator efficiency and the behaviors learned by robot policies. Workspace limitations, control-interface friction, and latency can introduce pauses, detours, and corrective motions into otherwise successful demonstrations.

We investigate these effects across embodiment, teleoperation control, and data consistency, combining a kinematic study of 25 dual-arm robots, controlled teleoperation experiments, and real-robot evaluation of fine-tuned $\pi_{0.5}$ policies.

The embodiment study shows that positional reachability overstates orientation-aware task coverage and that modest shoulder motion can substantially expand the effective workspace.

Teleoperation experiments show that parallelizing body-part control reduces task completion time by 43-53%, while compliant control improves success and reduces peak contact forces on constrained and contact-rich tasks.

The authors report that parallel control of body parts reduces task completion time, while compliant control improves success and lowers peak contact forces on tested constrained and contact-rich tasks. Active-search demonstrations improve arm-selection accuracy. In tested calibration configurations, inference-time miscalibration caused all trials to fail, and policies retained much of the extra path length in detour-contaminated demonstrations. These findings are bounded by the reported experiments.

sections.text:
Weight-space programming is a process where a large language model reads and writes the weights of a neural network directly, guided by a natural language specification, without an optimiser or gradient descent.

This study applies it to automatic tractor guidance, where a 253-parameter neural network steers along paths of lines and arcs and must be adapted when the machine changes, such as a slower steering actuator.

GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 (also 5.2) edited the network for our research tractor using a small budget of simulated evaluations to repair a network trained for another tractor and write a controller into a network with zero weights. We compared them with an evolution strategy, gradient descent and pure pursuit in simulation and on the real tractor.

Both models read the network and analysed the closed loop with control theory correctly, and Fable's repair without simulation succeeded only occasionally. With simulated feedback, both models repaired the trained network in single sessions and wrote a working controller from zero weights, whereas from zero the evolution strategy found none.

The controllers written from zero were sparse and in a classical cascaded structure; one model edited the trained network while the other replaced it. Gradient descent reached higher accuracy with far more simulation, and all language model controllers steered the real tractor without intervention, with errors of the same order as pure pursuit.

Language models can program the weights of a neural controller directly, much as control engineers design one. We call this Weight-Space Engineering.

summary.en: The study applies direct language-model editing of neural-network weights to tractor guidance. The authors report that, with limited simulated feedback, both tested models repaired a network trained for another tractor and wrote a working controller from zero weights; the evolution strategy found no controller from zero. Gradient descent achieved greater accuracy with substantially more simulation. On the real tractor, the language-model controllers steered without intervention, with errors reported to be of the same order as pure pursuit.

sections.text:
Conventional balance formulations often assume a rigid, stationary support, decoupling body stabilization from support motion. This assumption becomes inadequate on mechanically responsive supports, creating a coupled control challenge: corrective body motions intended to restore equilibrium can also excite support motion.

We formulate sustained balance as a coupled regulation problem that coordinates equilibrium restoration with suppression of motion induced by the robot's own corrections. We introduce LISST (Lyapunov-Inspired Sustained Stabilization), a learning framework that accounts for how earlier actions shape the conditions for subsequent corrections.

It uses recent observations to support immediate adjustments and longer histories to characterize persistent motion, with physical supervision relating the learned representation to robot-support behavior. To evaluate corrective actions, LISST uses coupled dynamics to assess both imbalance and the direction of motion.

A Lyapunov-inspired criterion measures progress over finite windows, accommodating the transients required to restore balance. This physical evaluation guides joint-level policy learning through backpropagation through differentiable model rollouts.

Privileged guidance focuses training on difficult states reached by the deployment policy and is transferred through distillation. The resulting policy operates using only onboard proprioception.

Real-world experiments demonstrate that LISST maintains balance while limiting residual oscillations during continuous interaction with a dynamically responsive support. Video: youtu.be/iGHU7S4wPyw.

summary.en: The paper presents LISST, a learning framework for balance on dynamically responsive supports. It treats balance as coupled regulation, accounting for both body imbalance and support motion induced by the robot’s corrections. Recent observations and longer histories inform a physically supervised representation; coupled dynamics and a finite-window, Lyapunov-inspired criterion guide policy learning. Privileged guidance is transferred through distillation, and the resulting policy uses onboard proprioception only. The authors report real-world experiments in which LISST maintained balance and limited residual oscillations during continuous interaction.

sections.text:
Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV) fleets in production and logistics environments rely on a system-wide emergency stop to handle local anomalies such as malfunctions, hazards, or contaminated areas. While safe, this approach halts the entire fleet even when only a small area is affected, causing unnecessary downtime.

This paper proposes dead zones -- a formally defined localized isolation approach that serves as an additional fail-operational mechanism for situations where a full system-wide halt is not strictly needed. Rather than shutting down the entire fleet, a dead zone isolates the anomalous area, allowing unaffected robots to continue operating normally.

We introduce two operational strategies: basic dead zone handling, in which affected robots enter a dead zone and stop, and dead zone handling with escaping, in which robots that are sufficiently far from a dead zone reroute around it.

For escaping on counterclockwise trajectories we prove collision-freedom with a bounded arrival delay for all escaping robots, provided a minimum pairwise separation is kept between robots.

Experimental evaluation confirms the theoretical guarantees and characterizes the throughput tradeoffs between all three approaches: full emergency stop, basic dead zone handling, and dead zone handling with escaping.

items.title: No Need to Stop the Fleet: Localized Anomaly Isolation via Dead Zones in AGV Fleets

World Action Models (WAMs) jointly generate future video and robot actions through iterative denoising. Few-step distillation reduces the number of model evaluations, but its coarse updates can move the student away from the teacher's trajectory.

We propose Anchored Path Matching (APM), which supervises endpoint and short-transition predictions from states reached by the student. From each state, we continue the teacher to zero noise and use its endpoint and first intermediate state as targets. Modality-routed adapters learn to match both targets from the same starting state.

When the two gradients conflict, anchor-priority updates preserve the endpoint gradient and remove the opposing component of the local gradient within each modality. One checkpoint supports 1-, 2-, and 4-step joint generation. The sampling budget can be chosen at deployment without retraining or teacher queries.

On RoboTwin 2.0, we train only on Clean demonstrations and evaluate directly on the domain-randomized Random setting. At one step, APM improves closed-loop success over continued base distillation at matched inference budgets by 2.0 percentage points on Clean and 1.4 on Random.

Video peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) rises from 30.169 to 32.317 dB, with gains in structural similarity (SSIM) and learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS).

On two real-robot tasks, APM improves success over the one-step teacher and reduces control-cycle latency by $21.3\times$ relative to the eight-step teacher.Project page: https://jialonglong.github.io/Anchored-Path-Matching/.

sections.text:
Generating a LEGO model from a user request is more than a plausible 3D shape generation. LEGO models require physical support per brick, and each brick should be placed unblocked. Current methods address this issue by training an expert large language model.

We reduce the problem of generating extremely long context on all brick connections to that of writing a program that builds LEGO models like a human, considering each intermediate step could be executed.

We introduce DailyBrick , a multi-stage agentic system that produces a LEGO model together with a brick-by-brick assembly instruction for human building and robot assembly. We design a multi-stage harness with roles to help LLMs generate more effectively.

A versioned construction SDK compiles multi-level decisions, from semantic subparts to individual bricks, into canonical operations.

An external Meta-Reviewer agent replays and inspects the generated package, verifies the model and its construction process, identifies failures, traces them to the responsible stage, and routes them to bounded repairs or to editable candidates for later skill or tool updates.

Extensive experiments demonstrate that DailyBrick generates LEGO models based on simple user requests better than recent agentic systems, and show its utility in downstream applications such as robot manipulations on model assembly from instructions and brick sets (https://SpatialAgent.github.io/DailyBrick/).

items.title: DailyBrick: Language-Guided Synthesis of Brick Assembly Instructions

sections.text:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models achieve high success rates on the LIBERO benchmark but remain sensitive to paraphrasing. Existing VLAs ranging from 0.6B to 7.5B parameters experience a 22-52 point performance drop on LIBERO-Para while SmolVLA exhibits an even larger decline, from 83\% to 8\%.

Because most VLAs jointly learn language understanding and action generation, it is difficult to determine whether a failure originates from misunderstanding an instruction or executing it incorrectly.

To address these challenges, we introduce CoBoVLA, or CodeBookVLA, a 250M-parameter VLA that decouples language understanding, planning, and control through learned discrete interpretable codes. A text encoder maps the instructions to shared step codes, which a visual planner then converts into action code sequences executed by a language-independent actor.

This design improves robustness to instruction paraphrasing while allowing failures to be traced to individual stages. It also enables efficient real-time control on resource-constrained hardware by encoding instructions only once and using compact discrete representations to keep each component lightweight.

CoBoVLA achieves 91.4\% success on LIBERO-Goal, compared with 82.8\% for SmolVLA, under a matched protocol, with 17 ms per control step latency. On LIBERO-Para, it achieves 81.1\% across 4,092 unseen paraphrases and 78.5\% on matched episodes, compared with 36.5\% for SmolVLA LoRA fine-tuned on paraphrases.

Without two-step demonstrations, CoBoVLA completes 48.8\% of 160 free-form two-step tasks. Finally, success reaches 91\% when instructions are correctly encoded but falls to 27.2\% otherwise, identifying language understanding as the main source of remaining failures.

Together, these results demonstrate that decoupling language understanding and control can improve instruction robustness while making VLA failures easier to diagnose.

items.title: CoBoVLA: Decoupling Language from Action with Discrete Codes for Robust and Interpretable Robot Manipulation

sections.text:
Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are often deployed as embodied controllers for robotics, yet it remains unclear how well they can explore an environment, maintain an internal map, and ground safety-critical decisions in long-horizon sequential trajectories.

In this work, we introduce EMRD, an evaluation framework that decouples spatial reasoning into four stages: Explore (what the agent observes), Map (what it records and where), Remember (what it retains), and Decide (whether its final choice is justified), scored across 18 stage-specific metrics.

We use EMRD to evaluate eleven open- and closed-weight VLMs across 16 buildings under nominal conditions and three environmental stresses (darkness, smoke, and motion noise), where an embodied VLM explores unknown rooms, maps observed objects, and selects the safest gathering place.

Open-weight models leave rooms unvisited in 95% of episodes and detect at most 51% of objects; closed-weight models explore more, though with an external memory (notepad), two of the three stop prematurely. Without external memory, most VLMs keep fewer of the objects they saw, especially in larger buildings.

The start limits which rooms are explored, and open-weight models started in different rooms agree on the final room not significantly more often than chance. Moreover, these choices are biased by semantic priors: swapping a room's label is often enough to change the final choice.

Finally, motion noise increases object position error (by 12-60% for closed-weight models), strong darkness lowers map recall by 28-31 percentage points, and dense smoke reduces seen objects by 25-39 points, while the choice among the rooms entered does not change significantly.

items.title: Explore, Map, Remember, Decide: A Benchmark for VLM Readiness in Safety-Critical Scenarios

While gravity is often used in mobile robotics as a global constraint for Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) algorithms, most estimation methods rely on indirect observation of the gravity vector. In this paper, we propose the use of altimeter measurements to directly observe the direction of the gravity vector.

We provide a theoretical evaluation of the estimation noise and validate it through extensive experimental data, along with an evaluation of the impact of intersensor distance on our gravity vector estimates. Experimental results demonstrate that a median error of $0.87^\circ$ on the tilt estimation can be achieved with our system in semi-static scenarios.

Furthermore, we demonstrate the potential of this approach by comparing it with state-of-the-art methods based on Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs).We highlight that we achieve similar performance to that of IMU-based systems in highly dynamic scenarios and even outperform in specific cases of accelerometer measurement saturation.

Finally, an additional experiment shows the potential use within a robotic system through the integration into an Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm.
